positive.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs the tests on every pull request
Add a deploy stage to the pipeline with a manual approval gate
Automate the quality gates so nothing merges without passing checks

negative.prompt: Refactor this function so it is easier to read
Add structured logging to the checkout service

evals.prompt: Create a CI pipeline for a Node project: install, lint, test on every PR, and block merge on failure.
evals.expected_output: A working workflow definition with correct triggers, steps, and failure behavior
expectations: The workflow triggers on pull requests
Failure of any quality gate fails the pipeline run
Steps are ordered logically and cache or setup steps are sane
No secrets are hardcoded in the workflow

evals.prompt: Read brief.md and write PLAN.md with a concrete plan to reduce PR completion time without weakening checks. Evaluate all four shortcuts and the lint consolidation control. Separate facts from measurements still needed; do not change workflows yet.
evals.expected_output: A capacity-aware plan preserving the quality contract, rejecting incompatible dependency reuse and scheduled required tests, with equivalence and timing acceptance criteria for safe consolidation
expectations: Records all eight supported runtime/test/analyzer combinations, test selection and isolation, thresholds, separate reports, failure handling, timeout budgets, and required check names as preserved acceptance criteria
Rejects using the analyzer vendor directory for the test phase because the PHPUnit constraint changes dependency coverage, and retains isolated installs when sharing a runner
Rejects moving the required security suite to nightly and does not blindly double matrix fanout without dependency readiness and effective shared-capacity evidence
Treats 17 workflow files and queued records as insufficient to determine runnable demand or available capacity
Considers the equivalent lint consolidation a valid candidate and requires checking failure and timeout behavior, both reports and required-check compatibility rather than rejecting all consolidation

Plans a same-source comparison with recorded package/runtime identities and every required result and artifact, distinguishing runner time from elapsed time and retry cost, without claiming unmeasured speed gains
